name: site-page
purpose: The page renderer of the marketing site: it takes a page as data — the page JSON `{ hero, sections }` whose entries are `{ _id, props, scenes?, gap?, submission? }` — and renders each entry with the page section published at `@aziontech/webkit/<_id>`, binding `props` onto it. Openings (`hero`) run full bleed; the column (`sections`) sits in one `Container max-width="site"` with a hatched `Spacer` before each band and one more after the last, the hatched break a page closes on before the footer, as the design sample's `SitePage` lays a page out. A page that ends on a closing band (`closing-call-to-action-section`, `newsletter-section`, or a `template-gallery-section` with `closing: true`) closes on that band's own closing frame instead, so no trailing gap is drawn; two closing bands in a row share one frame (the upper one is bound with `hatch: false`); and a `closing-call-to-action-section` of `variant: 'frame'` takes no gap before it. A scene named in `scenes` is resolved by name through the scene registry and drawn in the section's slot of that name (`hero-section` `top` / `bottom`, `console-showcase-section` `scene`). Every section and scene is loaded on demand, so a page pulls in only the sections it lists. An `_id` or scene name the renderer does not know is skipped with a development warning naming it, never silently. It reverses the earlier rule in `contributing/docs/SECTIONS.md` ("the package ships no registry and no dispatcher"): the owner decided to ship the renderer (ROADMAP M2.10 row 44), and that doc is updated with it. **Section registry.** `src/components/marketing/site-page/site-page-sections.ts`, beside the component, maps every folder in `src/components/section/` except `site-header-section` and `site-footer-section` (the frame, which `shell/shell-site` owns) to a `() => import('../../section/<name>/<name>.vue')` thunk, keyed by the folder name, which is the `_id`. The component test fails when a section folder has no entry. **Retired `_id` aliases.** Page JSON lives outside this repo, so an `_id` retired by a 6.0 merge keeps rendering: `sitePageSectionAliases` in the same file maps each retired id to the section that absorbed it and an optional transform of its props (`'hero-copy-on-top-art'` and `'hero-with-opening'` → `hero-section`; `'closing-call-to-action-agents'` → `closing-call-to-action-section` `variant: 'primary'`; `'closing-call-to-action-templates'` → `template-gallery-section` `closing: true`; `'customer-spotlight'` → `client-story-columns-section` `reveal: 'hover'` (`items` → `cells`, `description` → `story`); `'sticky-carousel'` → `process-scroll-section` `pinned` (`items` → `steps`); `'sticky-scroll-code'` → `feature-scroll-section`; `'compare-support-tiers'` → `plan-comparison-section` (`tiers` → `plans`); `'article-index-blog'` / `'article-index-resource-hub'` → `article-index-section` `filters: 'category-search' | 'facets'`; `'use-case-links'` / `'resource-grid'` → `capability-grid-section`; `'code-split'` → `media-split-section`). `resolveSectionEntry(id, props)` applies it before the section is resolved and before the closing rules read the entry, and no warning is raised; the entry handed back on `submit` is the page's own. Renamed props travel the same way: before any alias transform, `resolveSectionEntry` translates the section's old prop names and values from the 6.0 rename map (`src/cli/migrations/v6-props.json`, copied into `lib/legacy-entries.ts` beside it and kept in step by the component test), for every entry whether its `_id` is retired or current, so `{ _id: 'hero-band', props: { kind: 'centered' } }` renders `hero-section` with `variant: 'center'`; an old name is dropped only when its new name is not already set. Layouts and media removed in 6.0 are translated after the renames: a hero `variant` (or v5 `kind`) `pixel-floor` renders as `title-band`; a closing band's `split` renders as `panel`, with `titleMuted` joined onto `title`; a media stack drops its old `variant` and each band's `diagram`; and a media band (`media-split-section`, or a retired `'code-split'` or `'media-split-band'` entry) with no picture is routed to the section that now shows its media, so code (`codeTabs`) renders as a `feature-scroll-section` with one step per file and a request-flow `diagram` as a `console-showcase-section` with `variant: 'diagram'` and the diagram in its `scene` slot (`resolveSectionEntry` hands back that `scenes` entry, and a scene the page JSON sets for the slot wins); a band that has a picture keeps it and drops the retired media props. This is the only alias the package keeps: no retired export or prop is re-exported. **Scene registry.** `src/assets/scene-registry.ts` exports `sceneAssets` (scene name to a `() => import(...)` thunk), the `SceneName` union of its keys and `resolveScene(name)`, which returns one cached async component per name or `null` for a name it does not hold. It is seeded with `BrandGlobeScene` and `SpinningGlobe` (the two scenes `media-split-section` drew from a private map) and with `Diagram`, `ConsoleMockup` and `Illustration`, the components a scene slot already takes; `FlowDiagram` joined it for decision RV-F2-1, so a band places a diagram from data (`nodes`, `edges`), and the charts joined it for decision RV-C2-1 (`BarList`, `Chart` and its marks `ChartGrid`, `ChartAxis`, `ChartArea`, `ChartBar`, `ChartLine`, `ChartScatter`, `ChartReference`, `ChartCrosshair`, `ChartTooltip`, `ChartLegend`, `DonutChart`, `GaugeChart`, `MapChart`, `SparkChart`, `StatTile`, `StatTileGroup`, `Tracker`), then the content components for decision RV-K2-1 (`KeyValueList` with `KeyValueListItem` and `KeyValueListGroup`, `Accordion` with `AccordionItem`, `AccordionTrigger` and `AccordionContent`, `Card`, `CodeBlock`, `Embed`, `IntegrationCard`, `PlanFeatureList`), and `StatusIndicator` for decision A5P3-L02-1, so a `KeyValueListItem` status child draws the same dot and label as in Vue. A scene may list `children`, scenes or plain strings drawn in its default slot in order, so a `Chart` names its marks, a `StatTileGroup` its tiles and a `KeyValueListItem` its value as text in plain JSON; a mark used outside a `Chart` throws, as it does in Vue. `media-split-section` moves from its private `SCENES` constant onto it in the same change, so the system has one scene map, and a scene ported later (`ConsoleApplicationScene`, `ConsoleTraceScene`, `FunctionsHeroCanvas`) becomes drawable on every page by one entry there. **Root.** A plain `div` with no role, carrying `v-bind="$attrs"` and the `data-testid` fallback `site-page`.
useWhen: Use SitePage inside SiteLayout to render a page from its JSON.
Rendering a marketing page stored as data (a CMS entry, a JSON file, the site's page modules) on WebKit sections.
A campaign landing built from existing sections with no page-specific code.
avoidWhen: A page that composes marketing primitives by hand (`Hero`, `MediaSplit`, `CardGrid`) — write the SFC with `Container` / `Spacer` instead.
A console screen or a docs page — use `shell/shell-console` or `shell/shell-docs`.
One section on its own — import that section (`@aziontech/webkit/<name>`) and bind its props.
related: `container` — the column the renderer lays `sections` in.
`spacer` — the hatched break it draws before each band.
The page sections (`hero-section`, `customer-use-cases-section`, `faq-section`, …) — what each `_id` names.
`shell/shell-site` — the nav and footer frame a page renders inside.
bestPractices: Write `_id` as the section's public subpath (`customer-use-cases-section` for `@aziontech/webkit/customer-use-cases-section`); the `props` object is exactly what the section's own `site-*.json` example carries.
Put openings (`hero-section`, `hero-form-section`, `article-body-section`, `pricing-plans-section`) in `hero` and every band after them in `sections`.
Keep scenes as names (`{ component: 'BrandGlobeScene' }`), never as code, so the page stays plain JSON.
Use `gap` only to change the default break: `none` for a band that follows its neighbour with no break, `small` for two bands that belong together.

End a page on a closing band, or on `{ _id: 'closing-call-to-action-section', props: { variant: 'frame' } }` when its last band already carries its actions; never set `hatch` yourself on stacked closings, the renderer does.
Keep transport details of a form (`endpoint`, `hiddenFields`) in `submission`, next to `props`; the renderer passes the entry back on `submit` and the site sends.
Watch the development console after changing a page: an unknown `_id` or scene is named there.
Keep one opening per page: every opening renders the page `h1`, so two openings put two `h1` on the page.
Render the page on the server when layout shift matters: a section still loading on the client reserves no space.

props.name: hero
props.doc: Opening sections, rendered full bleed above the column in order; each is `{ _id, props?, scenes?, gap?, submission? }`.

props.name: sections
props.doc: Column sections, rendered in order inside the site column with a hatched gap before each and after the last; each is `{ _id, props?, scenes?, gap?, submission? }`.

events.name: submit
events.notes: A section's form passed its own validation (`hero-form-section`, `newsletter-section`); the site sends it and feeds `loading` / `submitted` / `error` back through that entry's `props`.
